one_liner: Sentry has a broad REST web API (v0) that uses self-serve auth tokens and OAuth. The vendor also runs an official hosted MCP server at mcp.sentry.dev. The fetched pages don't settle free-tier access details or the OAuth registration process.
auth_notes: The pages show that Sentry auth tokens exist, through a tutorial link on the API page. They also show that Sentry's hosted MCP server uses an OAuth flow against Sentry accounts. The API authentication page wasn't fetched. The earlier draft claim that OAuth requires partner registration came from a page that isn't in the provided set, so I dropped it. Composio lists a managed OAUTH2 scheme for Sentry. I kept OAUTH2 as primary on that hint, with low confidence. BASIC is excluded because the earlier source called legacy API keys deprecated, and that source isn't in the provided pages.
access_notes: The pages don't say anything about plan requirements. The docs describe auth tokens and a public API with no gating language. The earlier claim that a free tier works for testing came from a Nango page that isn't in the provided set, so it is unverified. I kept self_serve_free as the most defensible value, with low confidence.
blocker_notes: No blocker is visible in the provided pages. The details of OAuth app registration and plan-level API access are not confirmed by them.

evidence.quote: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically.
The current version of the Sentry's web API is considered **v0**.
Tutorial: Create a Sentry Authentication Token
The base MCP server address is: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`
All connections use OAuth. The first connection will trigger an authentication flow to connect to your Sentry account.
**yes, as the title of this post suggests - Sentry has an MCP server.**
